examples.trans: A language barrier will get in their way.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'barrier' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я бы сказал, языковой барьер помешает.
examples.trans: I would say a language barrier will get in the way.

examples.text: Языковой барьер им помешает.
examples.trans: A language barrier will get in their way.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мешать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will bother, hinder', paired with 'мешать'.

examples.text: Я бы сказал, языковой барьер помешает.
examples.trans: I would say a language barrier will get in the way.

examples.text: Языковой барьер им помешает.
examples.trans: A language barrier will get in their way.

examples.text: Извините, я вам сейчас не помешал?
examples.trans: Excuse me, did I interrupt you right now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, я сейчас.
examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.

examples.text: Подождите минуту.
examples.trans: Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'restroom' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Подожди меня, мне надо в туалет.
examples.trans: Wait for me, I need to go to the restroom.

examples.text: Где туалет?
examples.trans: Where's the toilet?

examples.text: Туалет в коридоре.
examples.trans: The toilet is in the corridor.
